widget.prompt: Why does area scale by the square of the scale factor?

authoredStages.title: Width stretches
authoredStages.body: Going from drawing to real, the width multiplies by the scale factor (say 4).

authoredStages.title: Height stretches too
authoredStages.body: The height also multiplies by 4 — both directions grow.

authoredStages.title: Area gets both
authoredStages.body: Area = width × height, so it picks up the factor twice: 4 × 4 = 16 times bigger.

widget.successFeedback: Exactly — area stretches in two directions at once, so the factor is squared.

explanationVariants: At 1 cm = 3 m, each cm² stands for 3 × 3 = 9 m².
Square the scale: 3² = 9 m² per cm².
